title: First Canadian Place
visualBrief: First Canadian Place after the 2012 recladding: rectangular notched plan, individually jointed white fritted-glass spandrels, bronze corner returns, paired vision lights, recessed colonnade, BMO crown panels and three detailed rooftop masts.

assembly.method: Repeated facade geometry uses EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing; canonical shared surfaces contain no embedded bitmap copies.

nativeAxes.longitudinal: +X east-northeast along the longer map axis
nativeAxes.origin: Cached tower footprint center at local ground contact; broader retail complex not yet registered.

reconstruction.planBasis: Owner level-27 plan shows approximately sixteen 10ft modules on north/south faces, fifteen on east/west faces and 15ft corner recesses. The inferred 190ft x180ft outer plan is close to the independently cached map envelope; not a dimensioned as-built survey.
reconstruction.floorBasis: Working office grid extrapolates the published average interval backwards from the highest occupied floor. Opaque crown replaces the upper main-face windows; corner glazing continues. Floor labels, roof/parapet datums and upper mechanical/occupied allocation are unverified.
reconstruction.materialBasis: Reusable opaque backed-glass triangular ceramic frit, shared stainless, painted metal, concrete, granite and marble. Frit pitch 50mm is inferred. Smooth glass has no height relief or copied photo texture.
reconstruction.roofBasis: Three-mast composition and guying follow original 2022 survey photographs. North tip uses the registry 355 m; other heights, positions, aerial details and roof plant are photograph reconstructions.

geographicProposal.reviewStatus: signed medium-fi owner north plan and photographed northern/southern masts
geographicProposal.orientationConfidence: owner plan and original signed rooftop photographs with raw QID outline
geographicProposal.notes: Fresh raw Q1052475 way 27767627 matches the independently preserved ground outline within 0.002 m projection rounding. Anchor [-79.381691573,43.648765146] and heading 0.277301287909 remain fixed: native +X ENE at 74.112 degrees and +Z SSE at 164.112 degrees. Actually inspected owner north-annotated level-27 plan supports the four corner recesses and independently inferred 190 ft by 180 ft office envelope. The original photographer labels the 355 m north mast and supplies a view from the geographically southwest CN Tower; that actual photograph shows the tall open northern lattice and shorter white-topped southern mast, signing the north/south rooftop allocation independently of the map rectangle. The model places those at [-7,-19] and [-7,19], with the shorter center mast [7,0]. Exact mast offsets and secondary tip height remain reconstructed. Street approaches and pier spacing are reconstructed within the tower envelope, not a surveyed entrance inventory. The fresh map also includes wider office outlines 61429747 and 366222382, but neither labels a complete measured FCP retail podium: one has layer 5 and the other an explicit subdivision warning. Those wider site masses are excluded from this tower asset rather than stretching the tower to them. Mapped 292 m is retained separately from registry architecture 298.1 m, tip 355 m and highest occupied floor 287.1 m; body parapet 289.9 m is the photographer working datum. Y0 is approximate entrance grade, without surveyed pavement slope. No footprint replacement.

scaleBasis: Published owner/architect/contractor heights and distinguishing construction systems; map footprint for local orientation, with reconstructed details declared separately.
geometrySource: Original deterministic exterior geometry; no downloaded meshes or copied photographic textures. Footprint-derived registration includes separately attributed OpenStreetMap evidence.
sourceLicense: Original reconstruction under repository license. Map-derived plan evidence: © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0. Reference publications are linked, not redistributed.
materialMethod: Canonical shared material graphs bound through molenSurface extras with metric coordinates divided by central repeat meters. Vertex colors provide component tint. Glass retains opaque metallic-roughness PBR; no bitmap texture copies per model.
reviewStatus: source-geometry; near/far and shared-material captures pending
limitations: The unchanged four-part GPU-instanced firstCanadianPlaceStudy.encodeAssembly remains the detailed source master. Runtime close-up reproduces all original geometry while combining opaque vision, bronze and backing surfaces into one tinted glass group. Six canonical graphs remain distinct for white fritted glass, stainless steel, painted metal, concrete, granite paving and marble lobby walls; with opaque and 52 percent clear palette glass this deliberately uses eight near groups, preserving visibly different architectural finishes rather than duplicating bitmaps. The preserved master has ten groups. Street retains every original office stripe and BMO vector mark, with a simpler recessed glazed lobby, whole piers and six-sided bollards; roof lattice stages, antennas and plant louvres are reduced. District retains each office stripe and all four corner steps, with sparse piers, closed mast envelopes and the round emblem in place of small wordmark strokes. Skyline merges five floor intervals into broad white/vision bands with the same area ratio; texture means are baked into one palette draw and small details are omitted. All levels retain the closed notched slab, crown, plant enclosure and three distinct masts. Owner modules, reconstructed 289.9 m body parapet, 298.1 m plant top, 355 m north tip and 351 m reconstructed south tip remain distinct. Average office spacing extrapolates floor datums; it does not survey every slab or confirm the allocation of marketed floor labels. Facade panel counts differ across publications, and the 50 mm triangular frit pitch is inferred. Exact door inventory, roof aerial layout and approximate BMO lettering are reconstructions. The model extent is the tower and its recessed colonnade within the mapped tower envelope; the broader retail/Exchange Tower complex is a separate site model and is excluded. Public raw adjacent outlines do not establish a surveyed retail boundary. Grade is approximate and no footprint replacement is used. Physical device and dense-city timing measurements remain pending.
importReason: Preserve thin facade frames, panel joints and crown/antenna details until a measured LOD chain is authored.
